title: Per-request KPI Hydrator and OTLP->Prometheus Deduper
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We currently ingest a mix of Prometheus-style scrapes and OTLP metric streams for inference requests. Downstream KPI consumers (dashboards, SLO rollups, billing) require deterministic per-request metrics (latency_ms, tokens_generated, model_variant, route) with cardinality controlled for tenant scale. Problem: duplicate signals appear when both the sidecar emits a per-request metric and the upstream proxy translates spans into OTLP metrics; we also see partial label mismatches (tenant_id vs org_id) and bursty high-cardinality from debug labels. Goal: implement a lightweight Hydrator component that canonicalizes per-request KPI envelopes, enriches with deterministic identifiers (request_id, tenant_digest), applies label canonicalization, and emits a single, deduplicated stream to Prometheus remote_write and to our metrics lake. The Hydrator will run as a small sidecar/agent in inference nodes and as an ingestion stage in the telemetry pipeline for hosted endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Hydrator accepts OTLP metrics and Prometheus packets and outputs a canonical per-request KPI envelope
Deduplication heuristic removes duplicate emissions where request_id matches and timestamps within 250ms
Label canonicalizer maps tenant_id, org_id, customer to a single tenant field; debug labels are filtered by sampling config
Output conforms to prometheus remote_write schema with fixed metric names: r_kpi_latency_ms, r_kpi_tokens, r_kpi_error_count
No >1% increase in pipeline tail-latency after enabling Hydrator in canary
Integration tests cover span->metric stitching, dedupe cases, and label normalization
implementation_steps: Design Hydrator schema and CEP (canonical envelope prototype) - document in Confluence
Build a minimal OTLP consumer that can parse gauge/counter/summary and map to envelope fields
Implement deterministic request_id extraction and tenant_digest algorithm
Add dedupe window implementation (configurable, default 250ms) with probabilistic memory cap per tenant
Wire outputs to Prometheus remote_write client and to existing metrics-lake Kafka topic
Create a canary deployment flow: edge nodes -> hydrator sidecar -> telemetry-staging -> dashboards
Run load tests with synthetic multi-tenant traffic to validate CPU/memory and dedupe effectiveness
Rollout plan: internal staging -> 5% production (non-critical customers) -> 25% -> 100%
Add monitoring and alerts for hydrator queue length, dedupe eviction rate, and label-loss rate
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff — scoped MVP schema, agreed on canonical metric names and minimal field set (request_id, tenant, model, route, latency_ms, tokens, error_flag).
2026-02-25: Design review with PM/Console team — decided to emit both Prometheus remote_write and a compact protobuf envelope to Kafka for downstream analytics. Runbooks drafted for canary rollback.

2026-03-02: PoC implemented — OTLP consumer can parse simple counters and create CEP; dedupe logic implemented using LRU cache per-tenant with TTL. Initial perf shows ~4% CPU overhead on a small node under synthetic load.
2026-03-08: Security review requested — data minimization confirmed (no PII collected); asked to surface KMS-backed tenant_digest option for private deployments.

2026-03-12: Met with Observability team — decided to increase dedupe window configurability and add a probabilistic Bloom filter fallback for very high-cardinality tenants to bound memory. Preparing canary PR.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs: strict deduping risks dropping legitimate rapid re-emissions for retried requests; to mitigate we include a routed_retry flag in envelope to bypass dedupe for known retries. Memory vs accuracy: LRU per-tenant is simple but can OOM under large tenants; chosen design adds tenant-level caps and Bloom filter fallback. We prioritized deterministic request_id extraction over probabilistic stitching to keep downstream billing and SLOs stable.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope mapping and label canonicalizer
Property-based tests for dedupe window with timestamp jitter
Integration test harness that replays production traces and validates 1:1 mapping for canonicalized requests
Performance test: sustained 20k req/s per node with sample tenants to ensure <1% pipeline latency regression
Canary observability: compare r_kpi_latency_ms p50/p95 between raw and hydrated streams and validate alerts
